mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.1% per annum signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 2.0% annualized inflation rate signals deteriorating real purchasing power, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns exceed 0% in > 50% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 and employment (PAYEMS) above 138,000 thousand units indicates robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO > 100 and PAYEMS > 138000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,050 thousand units signals weakening consumer confidence during late-cycle economic expansion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances where HOUST < 1050 during late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized rate indicates robust economic momentum, increasing corporate profitability and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of quarters where GDPC1 growth > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 6.5% signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 50% of periods where UNRATE > 6.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) above 426,000 million dollars and decreases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% indicate strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS > 426000 and FEDFUNDS < 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate increase above 0.5% per annum signals reduced liquidity, increasing equity risk premiums and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns exceed 0% in > 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% during tightening cycles.
